pages.name: Governance-overview
pages.title: SharePoint governance
pages.summary: What the governance service does and where to start.
sections:
What this site is for

SharePoint Online is governed as a business-as-usual service. The controls in the SharePoint Migration PID v4.2 are enforced by Power Automate flows that run on the lists on this site. You ask for something by adding an item to a list; the flow checks it, asks the right approvers and records the decision.

Start here

I need to…Do this
Get access to a site{{new:Access Requests|Raise an access request}}. See Request access for what is allowed.
Get a new site{{new:Site Requests|Raise a site request}}. See Request a site.
Review who can use my siteAnswer the review email. See Access reviews.
Decide on a file shareSee File shares.
Know who approves whatSee Roles.

The controls

FlowRunsControl it enforces
01 Access requestNew {{list:Access Requests}} itemThe Access Method Decision Table: service and shared accounts prohibited, staff without a Microsoft licence use the Base8 CMS in the Employee App, licence and Entra ID P2 checks, guests time-bound to 90 days, PIM for admins, group-based grants
02 Guest access expiryDaily 06:00Contractor guest access is time-bound and reviewed; the site owner decides removal unless the Board makes it automatic
03 Site provisioningNew {{list:Site Requests}} itemNaming standard, two named owners, permission groups, external sharing off by default
05 File share dispositionNew {{list:File Share Register}} itemFile shares move to SharePoint case by case only; system-dependent shares are excluded
06 Access recertificationMonthly, 1st, 07:0090-day review of site access, orphaned-site detection, quarterly review of privileged admin roles

Flow 04 (InfoPath triage) was retired on 25 October 2026. InfoPath forms are now triaged with the PID v4.2 Criticality Decision Tree through the programme's Flow 8.

Reading a status

Every Status column shows its value in a coloured box. The words always say what happened; the colour is a quick guide.

ColourMeansFor example
GreenGranted, approved or readyGranted; Provisioned; Ready for migration
RedBlocked, rejected, returned or failed: something needs fixing or was refusedBlocked - Licence required; Returned - Naming standard; Orphaned - owner inactive
BlueClosed with guidance, or a follow-up stepClosed - Use Employee App; Kept - owner decision; Read-only
GreyNot decided yetSubmitted; Removal pending owner decision; Awaiting owner decision

pages.name: Request-access
pages.title: Request access to a site
pages.summary: Which kinds of access are allowed and who approves them.
sections:
How to ask

{{new:Access Requests|Add an item to Access Requests}}: pick the site, your user type and a business justification. Flow 01 checks the request against the Access Method Decision Table and sends it to the approvers below. Access is always given through a security group, never to one person directly.

Access Method Decision Table

User typeWhat happensApproved by
Employee - view only (no Microsoft licence)Closed: use the Base8 CMS in the Employee AppNo approval
Employee - edit / collaborateNeeds an M365 licence that includes SharePoint (F3 or above), else Blocked - Licence requiredSite primary owner
Site Owner / AuthorNeeds a SharePoint licence (E3 or equivalent) and Entra ID P2, else BlockedLine manager and SharePoint service owner
Long-term contractorGuest access with an end date within 90 days, else Rejected - Not time-boundSite owner and InfoSec
Screen / kiosk / displayClosed: use the published display pageNo approval
Privileged adminIT Operations creates a PIM eligible assignmentInfoSec
Service / shared accountRejected - ProhibitedNot allowed

After approval

  • If the site's group is synced from on-premises AD, the Service Desk adds you to the AD group (status: Approved - awaiting AD group change).
  • Otherwise you are added to the Entra group straight away (status: Granted).
  • Contractor guests: the sponsor and site owner get one reminder 14 days before the end date. Renewing means a new access request, for 90 days at most. See Access reviews for what happens on the end date.

pages.name: Request-a-site
pages.title: Request a new site
pages.summary: What a new site needs and how it is set up.
sections:
Before you ask

  • A URL alias in lower case that follows the naming standard [org]-[location]-[department]-[site], with a known location code. Otherwise the request is Returned - Naming standard.
  • Two different, enabled, internal people as primary and secondary owner. Otherwise it is Returned - Ownership invalid.
  • An Owners group and a Members group (Entra object IDs). Visitors and Guests groups are optional.
  • A sensitivity: General, Confidential or Highly Confidential.
  • Whether you need external sharing. It is off unless approved.

Then {{new:Site Requests|add an item to Site Requests}}.

Who approves

  • The SharePoint service owner approves every new site.
  • InfoSec also approves when you ask for external sharing or the site is Highly Confidential.

What you get

Once the site is created, IT Operations applies and registers its Sites.Selected grant, then the baseline is applied: permissions through groups only, your secondary owner as a site admin, external sharing off unless approved, no custom script and your sensitivity label. Without the grant the request shows Provisioning failed and the service owner is told. The site is added to the {{list:Site Register}} with its first access review due in 90 days, and both owners are told.

pages.name: Access-reviews
pages.title: Access reviews
pages.summary: The 90-day review, orphaned sites and guest expiry.
sections:
90-day access review

On the 1st of each month, flow 06 emails the primary owner of every site whose review is due, listing its Owners and Members groups. Confirm the list is right, or say who should be removed. Removals go to the Service Desk. Every answer is logged and the next review is set for 90 days later.

Orphaned sites

If a site's primary owner account is no longer enabled, the site is marked Orphaned - owner inactive. The SharePoint service owner and IT Operations promote the secondary owner and name a new one.

Guest end dates

Guest access is recorded in the {{list:Guest Access Register}}. On the end date, the site owner or sponsor is asked to confirm removal:

  • Confirmed: the guest is removed from the site's Guests group and marked Expired - access removed; the sponsor, owner and InfoSec are told.
  • Not confirmed: access stays, the guest is marked Kept - owner decision and InfoSec is told. Continuing access needs a new access request.

If the Control Board rules expired guest access a critical class, removal on the end date becomes automatic.

Admin roles

In January, April, July and October, InfoSec confirms the SharePoint Admin role is PIM-eligible only.

pages.name: File-shares
pages.title: File shares
pages.summary: How remaining file shares are decided.
sections:
How a file share is decided

File shares move to SharePoint case by case. Each share in the {{list:File Share Register}} is checked in this order:

  1. An integration marker, app back-end or generic account: Excluded - system dependent. IT Operations agrees whether to remediate, archive, delete or move it to a non-SharePoint platform.
  2. Unmodified for 3 years or more: the owner is asked to approve archiving.
  3. Otherwise the owner and the SharePoint service owner approve migration. Shares with High permission complexity have their permissions remediated first.

pages.name: Governance-roles
pages.title: Governance roles
sections:
Roles

The flows send approvals to roles, not named people, so a change of staff only changes a setting.

RoleApproves or receives
SharePoint service ownerApproves new sites and file share migrations; second approver for Site Owner / Author access; receives provisioning failures and orphaned-site alerts
Security and Architecture (InfoSec)Approves guest access, privileged admin roles, and sites with external sharing or Highly Confidential content; quarterly admin-role review
IT Operations ownerApplies and registers the Sites.Selected grant for each new site; creates PIM assignments; agrees dispositions for excluded file shares and permission remediation; orphaned-site alerts
Service DeskFulfilment tickets: AD group changes and access removals
